claims.claim: Tempo is the rate or relative speed at which a musical pulse moves through time.
A metronome marking specifies the rate of a designated note value in beats per minute, and MM=120 indicates 120 pulse beats per minute.
Verbal markings such as adagio, andante, allegro, and presto give relative pace or character cues rather than a fixed BPM that applies identically to every composer and piece.
Accelerando indicates a gradual increase in tempo, while ritardando and rallentando indicate gradual slowing in the cited introductory sources.
Tempo is distinct from meter because tempo gives the rate of beats and meter gives their grouping; changing rate does not by itself change the grouping.
Perceived speed can depend on beat rate as well as texture, complexity, and frequency of subdivisions, so event density alone is not sufficient evidence for a tempo change.
